questions.question: What is an effect of excessive phase noise in an SDR receiver’s master clock oscillator?

choices.A: It limits the receiver’s ability to receive strong signals
choices.B: It can affect the receiver’s frequency calibration
choices.C: It decreases the receiver’s third-order intercept point
choices.D: It can combine with strong signals on nearby frequencies to generate interference

questions.answer: It can combine with strong signals on nearby frequencies to generate interference

questions.question: Which of the following receiver circuits can be effective in eliminating interference from strong out-of-band signals?

choices.A: A front-end filter or preselector
choices.B: A narrow IF filter
choices.C: A notch filter
choices.D: A properly adjusted product detector

questions.answer: A front-end filter or preselector

questions.question: What is the term for the suppression in an FM receiver of one signal by another stronger signal on the same frequency?

choices.A: Desensitization
choices.B: Cross-modulation interference
choices.C: Capture effect
choices.D: Frequency discrimination

questions.answer: Capture effect

questions.question: What is the noise figure of a receiver?

choices.A: The ratio of atmospheric noise to phase noise
choices.B: The ratio of the noise bandwidth in hertz to the theoretical bandwidth of a resistive network
choices.C: The ratio in dB of the noise generated in the receiver to atmospheric noise
choices.D: The ratio in dB of the noise generated by the receiver to the theoretical minimum noise

questions.answer: The ratio in dB of the noise generated by the receiver to the theoretical minimum noise

questions.question: What does a receiver noise floor of -174 dBm represent?

choices.A: The receiver noise is 6 dB above the theoretical minimum
choices.B: The theoretical noise in a 1 Hz bandwidth at the input of a perfect receiver at room temperature
choices.C: The noise figure of a 1 Hz bandwidth receiver
choices.D: The receiver noise is 3 dB above theoretical minimum

questions.answer: The theoretical noise in a 1 Hz bandwidth at the input of a perfect receiver at room temperature

questions.question: How much does increasing a receiver’s bandwidth from 50 Hz to 1,000 Hz increase the receiver’s noise floor?

choices.A: 3 dB
choices.B: 5 dB
choices.C: 10 dB
choices.D: 13 dB

questions.answer: 13 dB

questions.question: What does the MDS of a receiver represent?

choices.A: The meter display sensitivity
choices.B: The minimum discernible signal
choices.C: The modulation distortion specification
choices.D: The maximum detectable spectrum

questions.answer: The minimum discernible signal

questions.question: An SDR receiver is overloaded when input signals exceed what level?

choices.A: One-half of the maximum sample rate
choices.B: One-half of the maximum sampling buffer size
choices.C: The maximum count value of the analog-to-digital converter
choices.D: The reference voltage of the analog-to-digital converter

questions.answer: The reference voltage of the analog-to-digital converter

questions.question: Which of the following choices is a good reason for selecting a high IF for a superheterodyne HF or VHF communications receiver?

choices.A: Fewer components in the receiver
choices.B: Reduced drift
choices.C: Easier for front-end circuitry to eliminate image responses
choices.D: Improved receiver noise figure

questions.answer: Easier for front-end circuitry to eliminate image responses

questions.question: What is an advantage of having a variety of receiver bandwidths from which to select?

choices.A: The noise figure of the RF amplifier can be adjusted to match the modulation type, thus increasing receiver sensitivity
choices.B: Receiver power consumption can be reduced when wider bandwidth is not required
choices.C: Receive bandwidth can be set to match the modulation bandwidth, maximizing signal-to-noise ratio and minimizing interference
choices.D: Multiple frequencies can be received simultaneously if desired

questions.answer: Receive bandwidth can be set to match the modulation bandwidth, maximizing signal-to-noise ratio and minimizing interference

questions.question: Why does input attenuation reduce receiver overload on the lower frequency HF bands with little or no impact on signal-to-noise ratio?

choices.A: The attenuator has a low-pass filter to increase the strength of lower frequency signals
choices.B: The attenuator has a noise filter to suppress interference
choices.C: Signals are attenuated separately from the noise
choices.D: Atmospheric noise is generally greater than internally generated noise even after attenuation

questions.answer: Atmospheric noise is generally greater than internally generated noise even after attenuation

questions.question: How does a narrow-band roofing filter affect receiver performance?

choices.A: It improves sensitivity by reducing front-end noise
choices.B: It improves intelligibility by using low Q circuitry to reduce ringing
choices.C: It improves blocking dynamic range by attenuating strong signals near the receive frequency
choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.answer: It improves blocking dynamic range by attenuating strong signals near the receive frequency

questions.question: What is reciprocal mixing?

choices.A: Two out-of-band signals mixing to generate an in-band spurious signal
choices.B: In-phase signals cancelling in a mixer resulting in loss of receiver sensitivity
choices.C: Two digital signals combining from alternate time slots
choices.D: Local oscillator phase noise mixing with adjacent strong signals to create interference to desired signals

questions.answer: Local oscillator phase noise mixing with adjacent strong signals to create interference to desired signals

questions.question: What is the purpose of the receiver IF Shift control?

choices.A: To permit listening on a different frequency from the transmitting frequency
choices.B: To change frequency rapidly
choices.C: To reduce interference from stations transmitting on adjacent frequencies
choices.D: To tune in stations slightly off frequency without changing the transmit frequency

questions.answer: To reduce interference from stations transmitting on adjacent frequencies

questions.question: What is meant by the blocking dynamic range of a receiver?

choices.A: The difference in dB between the noise floor and the level of an incoming signal that will cause 1 dB of gain compression
choices.B: The minimum difference in dB between the levels of two FM signals that will cause one signal to block the other
choices.C: The difference in dB between the noise floor and the third-order intercept point
choices.D: The minimum difference in dB between two signals which produce third-order intermodulation products greater than the noise floor

questions.answer: The difference in dB between the noise floor and the level of an incoming signal that will cause 1 dB of gain compression

questions.question: Which of the following describes problems caused by poor dynamic range in a receiver?

choices.A: Spurious signals caused by cross modulation and desensitization from strong adjacent signals
choices.B: Oscillator instability requiring frequent retuning and loss of ability to recover the opposite sideband
choices.C: Poor weak signal reception caused by insufficient local oscillator injection
choices.D: Oscillator instability and severe audio distortion of all but the strongest received signals

questions.answer: Spurious signals caused by cross modulation and desensitization from strong adjacent signals

questions.question: What creates intermodulation interference between two repeaters in close proximity?

choices.A: The output signals cause feedback in the final amplifier of one or both transmitters
choices.B: The output signals mix in the final amplifier of one or both transmitters
choices.C: The input frequencies are harmonically related
choices.D: The output frequencies are harmonically related

questions.answer: The output signals mix in the final amplifier of one or both transmitters

questions.question: Which of the following is used to reduce or eliminate intermodulation interference in a repeater caused by a nearby transmitter?

choices.A: A band-pass filter in the feed line between the transmitter and receiver
choices.B: A properly terminated circulator at the output of the repeater’s transmitter
choices.C: Utilizing a Class C final amplifier
choices.D: Utilizing a Class D final amplifier

questions.answer: A properly terminated circulator at the output of the repeater’s transmitter

questions.question: What is the term for the reduction in receiver sensitivity caused by a strong signal near the received frequency?

choices.A: Reciprocal mixing
choices.B: Quieting
choices.C: Desensitization
choices.D: Cross modulation interference

questions.answer: Desensitization

questions.question: Which of the following reduces the likelihood of receiver desensitization?

choices.A: Insert attenuation before the first RF stage
choices.B: Raise the receiver’s IF frequency
choices.C: Increase the receiver’s front-end gain
choices.D: Switch from fast AGC to slow AGC

questions.answer: Insert attenuation before the first RF stage

questions.question: What causes intermodulation in an electronic circuit?

choices.A: Negative feedback
choices.B: Lack of neutralization
choices.C: Nonlinear circuits or devices
choices.D: Positive feedback

questions.answer: Nonlinear circuits or devices

questions.question: What is the purpose of the preselector in a communications receiver?

choices.A: To store frequencies that are often used
choices.B: To provide broadband attenuation before the first RF stage to prevent intermodulation
choices.C: To increase the rejection of signals outside the band being received
choices.D: To allow selection of the optimum RF amplifier device

questions.answer: To increase the rejection of signals outside the band being received

questions.question: What does a third-order intercept level of 40 dBm mean with respect to receiver performance?

choices.A: Signals less than 40 dBm will not generate audible third-order intermodulation products
choices.B: The receiver can tolerate signals up to 40 dB above the noise floor without producing third-order intermodulation products
choices.C: A pair of 40 dBm input signals will theoretically generate a third-order intermodulation product that has the same output amplitude as either of the input signals
choices.D: A pair of 1 mW input signals will produce a third-order intermodulation product that is 40 dB stronger than the input signal

questions.answer: A pair of 40 dBm input signals will theoretically generate a third-order intermodulation product that has the same output amplitude as either of the input signals

questions.question: Why are odd-order intermodulation products, created within a receiver, of particular interest compared to other products?

choices.A: Odd-order products of two signals in the band being received are also likely to be within the band
choices.B: Odd-order products are more likely to overload the IF filters
choices.C: Odd-order products are an indication of poor image rejection
choices.D: Odd-order intermodulation produces three products for every input signal within the band of interest

questions.answer: Odd-order products of two signals in the band being received are also likely to be within the band

questions.question: What is the link margin in a system with a transmit power level of 10 W (+40 dBm), a system antenna gain of 10 dBi, a cable loss of 3 dB, a path loss of 136 dB, a receiver minimum discernable signal of -103 dBm, and a required signal-to-noise ratio of 6 dB?

choices.A: -8dB
choices.B: -14dB
choices.C: +8dB
choices.D: +14dB

questions.answer: +8dB

questions.question: What is the received signal level with a transmit power of 10 W (+40 dBm), a transmit antenna gain of 6 dBi, a receive antenna gain of 3 dBi, and a path loss of 100 dB?

choices.A: -51 dBm
choices.B: -54 dBm
choices.C: -57 dBm
choices.D: -60 dBm

questions.answer: -51 dBm

questions.question: What power level does a receiver minimum discernible signal of -100 dBm represent?

choices.A: 100 microwatts
choices.B: 0.1 microwatt
choices.C: 0.001 microwatts
choices.D: 0.1 picowatts

questions.answer: 0.1 picowatts
